correctness.rationale: For all n>=4 and positive λ, directly compare rim payoffs: agreeing with hub requires two opposing rim neighbors; opposing hub requires at least one agreeing rim neighbor precisely below λ=2, while at equality it has no additional requirement. Hence the hub-agreeing set is exactly maximal independent / arbitrary independent / empty in three regimes, and hub stability follows from independence size <=n/2. Cyclic gaps 2 or 3 establish counts and size-refined formula, using explicitly credited known Perrin/Lucas independent-set enumerations. For any cut with k rim vertices opposing hub, its rim contribution is at most 2 min(k,n-k), yielding OPT and a sharp PoA<=3/2 with λ->0 and n multiple 6. No finite enumeration is used to infer the infinite result; 98,112 exact-rational direct-game tests supplement the proof.

value.rationale: A natural one-hub social game with ring interactions has an exact, all-size equilibrium entropy phase transition: 2 Perrin, 2 Lucas, then 2 pure states at one sharp ratio. The characterization also gives the complete welfare spectrum, all weights with zero inefficiency, and sharp worst-case 3/2 price of anarchy, clarifying equilibrium abundance versus optimality. This combines structural dynamical-game meaning with a nontrivial full infinite-family classification and is not merely recounting a classical independent-set table.
